title: Chain conditions and preservation

based_on.title: Set Theory

based_on.title: Forcing Summer School Lecture Notes
based_on.pages: 39 (§13, cardinal preservation; singular-cardinal supremum inference replaced by a union-cardinality argument)

summary: Use countable antichains of deciding conditions to preserve every cardinal and cofinality, including at singular cardinals.
abstract: Adding a new subset of the natural numbers need not collapse an old cardinal or change the length of a shortest cofinal sequence. A sufficient condition is that every antichain of forcing conditions be countable inside the ground model. For one named ordinal, a maximal antichain of deciding conditions then gives a countable ground set containing every possible value. Applying this to each coordinate of a named function bounds its range by a ground union of countable sets. The resulting cardinal estimate preserves all cardinals, including singular ones, and a separate boundedness argument preserves cofinalities. Finite binary partial functions satisfy this chain condition, so these conclusions apply even when their generic union is a new binary sequence.
